- 在留外国人については、日本に在留する外国人数が過去最多を更新（10月17日）と報じられています。
- 法制度では、カスハラ対策を企業に義務付け、顧客による暴言など（10月1日）が話題になりました。

**経済**
- ビール税率が一本化、ビールは値下げ、発泡酒は値上げ（10月1日）となりました。
- ニデックが5000億円超の赤字、監査法人は意見表明せず（10月1日）と伝えられています。
- サイゼリヤ、メニュー８割強を値上げ　２９日に、コスト上昇でとの発表がありました。
- 公正取引委員会は、ビールのカルテルをめぐって地方の営業所も含めて強制調査を行いました。
- 金融庁は、プルデンシャル生命に対して業務停止命令を出しました(金融庁がプルデンシャル生命に業務停止命令（10月9日）)。

- 政府は、政府、漫画・アニメを外交活用　「日本ファン」新興国で拡大狙うという方針を示しています。

Here are the main Japan stories from my search, mostly from October 12-16, 2026.

**Politics and local government**
- The Yokohama mayoral race is being shaped by a power-harassment controversy involving former mayor Takeharu Yamanaka, and by renewed debate over a possible casino development. While Takeharu Yamanaka promised to change his behavior, he has also rekindled the question of, and his opposition to, a potential casino development.
- Mie Prefecture's assembly approved what officials say is Japan's first local ordinance with penalties for customer harassment. According to the prefectural government, it is the first ordinance in Japan to impose penalties for customer harassment.
- The Cabinet approved a bill that would let authorities remotely access devices used by criminal groups. Authorities are seeking to counter encrypted messaging and prevent fraud, robbery and other offenses.

**Courts**
- The Nagoya District Court dismissed a lawsuit that was filed on paper, because the digital civil litigation rules require legal representatives to submit court documents online. The lawsuit was thrown out by the Nagoya District Court under rules requiring legal representatives to submit civil court documents online.

**Economy**
- According to people familiar with the matter, Bank of Japan officials are reportedly leaning against a back-to-back rate hike this month, while still considering another move as early as December. Bank of Japan officials are leaning against a rare back-to-back interest rate increase this month while still eyeing the possibility of another move as soon as December, according to people familiar with the matter.

**Cybersecurity**
- Japan has seen a wave of data breaches. Between late September and early October 2026, Japanese companies and public bodies disclosed one breach after another. TV Asahi counted more than 40 announcements in about a month.
- One large incident was a ransomware attack on IDC Frontier's cloud region. IDC Frontier: ransomware stops part of its IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1 at about 03:40. 495 companies and local governments are affected.
- Ransomware reports are at a high. 123 Ransomware cases reported to police in the first half of 2026, a record
- The government has not said whether a nation-state is behind the attacks. The government has not drawn a conclusion.

**Security and diplomacy**
- Prime Minister Takaichi issued instructions responding to a suspected North Korean ballistic missile launch on October 12, after a similar response on October 3. October 12, 2026 Statements Instructions by the Prime Minister in Response to the Suspected Ballistic Missile Launch by North Korea (09:24)
- The Prime Minister also commented on a Nobel Prize in Chemistry awarded to a Japanese researcher. October 7, 2026 Statements Comment by Prime Minister Takaichi on the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026

**Other**
- A headline on a Toyota-related page mentions a false earthquake alert: Nerves rattled in Japan as alert for magnitude 9.9 quake withdrawn minutes later. The snippet gives no further detail, so I couldn't confirm the specifics.

Some items in the results were older or irrelevant, such as 2025 TV listings and a blog comment thread, so I left them out. For the full picture, the Japan Times latest-news page and the Prime Minister's Office news page are the best places to check.

Yana Offers to Resign","url":"https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2026101401069/"}]

Takaichi didn't formally fire Agriculture Minister Kazuo Yana. He resigned under pressure, which media describe as an effective dismissal. The search results describe the sequence this way:

- **The scandal:** Yana stepped down on Wednesday after coming under fire for remarks about cutting road funding for municipalities that did not support him. It has been learned that Yana's camp provided supporters with free shuttle bus transportation during the campaign period for the House of Representatives election in February, in possible violation of the public offices election law.
- **Takaichi's position:** She accepted Yana's resignation because the government "needs to work on important issues," mentioning legislation on a proposed consumption tax rate cut for food. She also had openly chided him in parliament for the remarks over the road funding before he left.
- **Opposition pressure:** Opposition parties in the upper house, where the ruling coalition lacks a majority, were preparing a censure motion against Yana, while some threatened to block debate on the sales tax legislation until he stepped down.
- **Accountability:** Takaichi said responsibility for appointing him (to the post) rests upon me, the prime minister.
- **Replacement:** On Thursday, Takaichi said she had offered Arata Takebe the post of farm minister, citing his policy expertise and parliamentary experience.

This was the first scandal-related departure of a cabinet member since the Takaichi administration was launched in October last year.

2026年10月16日に気象庁が出した緊急地震速報(警報)は、実際はカムチャツカ半島付近の地震(M6.9)を、千島列島の地震(M9.9)と誤って推定したものでした。

**経緯**
- 気象庁は、16日午後0時40分、北海道から東海地方にかけて最大震度7の地震が起きるとする緊急地震速報を出し、同48分に取り消したとされています。
- 実際の地震はカムチャツカ半島付近を震源とするM6.9の地震で、国内で観測された最大震度は1だったとのことです。
- 「警報」の取り消しは今回が初めてだと報じられています。「予報」の取り消しは過去にもありました。

**原因**
- 気象庁は、実際の震源よりおよそ680キロ離れた地点で地震が発生したとして計算したことが要因だと説明しています。
- 気象庁の資料では、震源から遠い観測点をマグニチュードの計算に用いたことにより、地震の規模をマグニチュード9.9と過大に推定したことが原因の一つとされています。
- 過去の事例(2020年の鳥島近海の地震)を受けて、震源から700㎞以上遠い観測点をマグニチュードの計算に用いないこととしていましたが、今回はこの機能が正常に動作していなかったことが判明しました。
- 別の報道では、震源を2回誤ってマグニチュードなどを算出していたことも原因として挙げられています。

**その他**
- 気象庁は記者会見で謝罪しました。サイバー攻撃の可能性は「ない」と明言したとも報じられています。
- 報道によると、国内で震度2以上を観測した場所はなかったとのことです。

なお、報道によって時刻の表記に差があります(発表は12時40分、取り消しは12時48分ごろとする報道が多いです)。詳細は気象庁の公式発表でご確認ください。

- 「警報」の取り消しは今回が初めてだと報じられています。「予報」の取り消しは過去にもありました。

**原因**
- 気象庁は、実際の震源よりおよそ680キロ離れた地点で地震が発生したとして計算したことが要因だと説明しています。
- 気象庁の資料では、震源から遠い観測点をマグニチュードの計算に用いたことにより、地震の規模をマグニチュード9.9と過大に推定したことが原因の一つとされています。
- 過去の事例(2020年の鳥島近海の地震)を受けて、震源から700㎞以上遠い観測点をマグニチュードの計算に用いないこととしていましたが、今回はこの機能が正常に動作していなかったことが判明しました。
- 別の報道では、震源を2回誤ってマグニチュードなどを算出していたことも原因として挙げられています。

**その他**
- 気象庁は記者会見で謝罪しました。サイバー攻撃の可能性は「ない」と明言したとも報じられています。
- 報道によると、国内で震度2以上を観測した場所はなかったとのことです。

なお、報道によって時刻の表記に差があります(発表は12時40分、取り消しは12時48分ごろとする報道が多いです)。詳細は気象庁の公式発表でご確認ください。

Here are what I judge to be the three biggest Japan stories from October 12–19, 2026:

1. **Farm minister resigns:** Agriculture Minister Kazuo Yana stepped down on October 14, which amounted to a forced dismissal and was the first scandal-driven exit from Prime Minister Takaichi's cabinet. He had been criticized for remarks about cutting road funding to municipalities that didn't back him, and opposition parties threatened to stall the consumption-tax-cut bill until he left. [Nippon.com / Jiji](https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2026101400736/)

2. **False magnitude 9.9 earthquake alert:** On October 16 the Japan Meteorological Agency issued an emergency earthquake warning predicting shaking up to intensity 7 from Hokkaido to Tokai, then withdrew it about eight minutes later. It was the first time a full "warning" has been cancelled; the real quake was an M6.9 near Kamchatka, and the agency apologized, blaming a miscalculation and ruling out a cyberattack. [Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbun (Japanese)](https://kumanichi.com/articles/2047238)

3. **Bank of Japan rate outlook:** On October 13 the Japan Times reported that, according to people familiar with the matter, Bank of Japan officials are leaning against raising rates again this month but could raise them as early as December. [The Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/10/13/economy/boj-lean-against-october-rate-hike/)

Other notable stories this week included North Korea's suspected ballistic missile launch on October 12 and figures released October 17 showing a record number of foreign residents in Japan.
